clue.text: A record capturing French horn concert

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: to capture something is to hold it inside, so one piece goes within the others

parts.note: a compact disc is a record
cor is the French word for horn

explanation.surface: A recording of a French horn concert being made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Concert' looks like part of the musical picture, but it is the definition in its sense of agreement, as in acting in concert.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting in concert means acting in agreement, which is a synonym of being in accord.

clue.text: President Cleveland's face has moustache, perhaps

indicators.note: the face of something is its front, so only the opening letter is wanted

parts.note: the first letter of Cleveland
a moustache is an example of facial hair, hence 'perhaps'

explanation.surface: A remark on whether US President Grover Cleveland sported a moustache.
explanation.walkthrough: President Cleveland seems one unit, but 'President' alone is the definition, as the person presiding over a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Whoever presides over a committee or meeting is called its chair, a synonym of president.

clue.text: Punk's too giddy about leading part for Emily Blunt

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the jumbled letters go round the single letter

parts.note: the letters of punk's and too

indicators.note: the leading part of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of Emily

explanation.surface: A dizzy punk fan hankering after a starring role for the actress Emily Blunt.
explanation.walkthrough: Emily Blunt looks like the actress's name, but the surname is the definition, as the adjective for frank speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A blunt person speaks frankly without softening things, which is a synonym of outspoken.

clue.text: Fake revolutionary hears about new beliefs

indicators.note: a revolution turns something round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: cod is an adjective meaning sham or mock, as in cod science

indicators.note: about means going round, so the verb surrounds the single letter

parts.note: a court hears or tries a case
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A phoney revolutionary listens to talk of new ideologies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fake revolutionary' reads as a person, but it is cod, meaning bogus, turned round; the judicial sense of hears supplies the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Doctrines are sets of principles held and taught, so beliefs is a fair plural synonym.

clue.text: Bluster and just beat European launcher of darts

parts.note: to bluster, of wind, is to blow
to pip is to beat narrowly
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A darts player who blustered and narrowly beat a European opponent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Launcher of darts' suggests the pub game, but the darts here are the small missiles of a hunting tube.
explanation.definitionFit: A blowpipe is a tube through which a hunter blows small poisoned darts at prey.

clue.text: Agile climber to stand around base of Everest

parts.note: to bear something is to stand or tolerate it
ca. (circa) is the abbreviation for around, as with dates

parts.note: the last letter of Everest

explanation.surface: A nimble mountaineer pausing near the foot of Everest.
explanation.walkthrough: The mountaineering surface makes 'climber' sound like a person; it is a tree-climbing mammal of Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: The bearcat, or binturong, is a tree-dwelling mammal of South-East Asia that climbs nimbly through the forest.

clue.text: Applaud tax-free drug?

parts.note: free of tax is zero VAT, O being zero and VAT the British sales tax
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A cheer for a medicine sold without tax.
explanation.walkthrough: VAT is value added tax, Britain's sales tax; nought VAT means none. The verb is a jokey back-formation from ovation, which Chambers lists.
explanation.definitionFit: To ovate is to give an ovation, a humorous verb formed from the noun for loud public applause.

clue.text: After four failed schemes, devise this carpentry tool?

parts.note: a plan is a scheme
if plans A, B, C and D have all failed, the next one is plan E

explanation.surface: Advice to a frustrated woodworker: after four schemes fall through, make a smoothing tool.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is in the lettered plans: after Plan A through Plan D fail, the next scheme to devise is the fifth letter's plan.
explanation.definitionFit: A plane is a hand tool a carpenter pushes along wood to shave and smooth its surface.

clue.text: E.g. perfect way to stop secretary suffering anxiety

indicators.note: a stop closes something off, so the street comes at the end of the secretary as its last part

parts.note: PA is a personal assistant, a secretary
St is the abbreviation for street, a way
someone tense is suffering anxiety

explanation.surface: Advice on the ideal method for keeping a secretary from getting stressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perfect' reads as an adjective meaning ideal; it is the grammatical tense. 'To stop' places the street after the secretary, closing that piece.
explanation.definitionFit: The perfect is a grammatical tense describing completed action, and in English it is a form of past tense.

clue.text: Man in red suit drops off US gunners in city there

indicators.note: drops off means lets fall away, so those letters are removed from the figure

parts.note: Father Christmas wears a red suit
taken as written, the letters to lose
RA is the Royal Artillery, the gunners

explanation.surface: Santa leaves American artillerymen in a city somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the clue: 'there' points back to the US, so the city is one in America.
explanation.definitionFit: Santa Clara is a city in California's Silicon Valley, so it is a city in the US named earlier.

clue.text: Artist going over silhouette of Sneezy and Grumpy

indicators.note: going over suggests turning over, so the word is read backwards

indicators.note: a silhouette is just an outline, so only the outside letters are kept

parts.note: the outside letters of Sneezy

explanation.surface: An artist sketching the outlines of two of Snow White's seven dwarfs.
explanation.walkthrough: Grumpy looks like the next dwarf after Sneezy, but it is the definition. Arsy is British slang for bad-tempered or awkward.
explanation.definitionFit: Arsy is informal British for irritable and difficult, so it is a slang synonym of grumpy.

clue.text: Music expert building material about Bach's final restoration of harmony

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the building material goes round the letter

parts.note: rap is a genre of music
a pro is an expert
cement is a building material

indicators.note: final points to the closing letter of the composer's name

parts.note: the last letter of Bach

explanation.surface: A musicologist builds a case about how Bach's last work restores harmony.
explanation.walkthrough: Bach and harmony make the clue sound musical, but harmony here means good relations between parties.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapprochement is the re-establishment of friendly relations, especially between nations, so it restores harmony.

clue.text: Posh partner mostly working, making gesture

parts.note: Becks is the nickname of footballer David Beckham, husband of Victoria, Posh Spice
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: Posh Spice's husband, mostly busy, waves a hand.
explanation.walkthrough: Posh is Victoria Beckham's Spice Girls nickname, and her husband David is widely called Becks.
explanation.definitionFit: To beckon is to gesture with the hand or head to call someone over, so gesture works as a verb.

clue.text: Naturalist's Tibetan animal in northerly green, rolling lea

parts.note: the letters of lea, a meadow
a zo, or dzo, is a Himalayan cross between a yak and a cow

explanation.surface: A wildlife expert describes a yak-like beast on green, undulating pasture.
explanation.walkthrough: Naturalist suggests a nature lover; the French novelist was the leader of the naturalist school of writing.
explanation.definitionFit: Émile Zola was the chief exponent of literary naturalism, the realist novel movement of nineteenth-century France.

clue.text: As I see it, British soldier drops minute object

indicators.note: drops means lets go of, so that letter is removed from the soldier

parts.note: Tommy is the traditional nickname for a British private soldier
M is the abbreviation for minute, the letter removed
to mind is to object, as in 'do you mind?'

explanation.surface: In my view, a British soldier lets fall a tiny item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minute object' reads as a tiny thing, but minute is the abbreviation removed and object is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase introduces a personal opinion, just as 'as I see it' does; it is an idiom synonym.

clue.text: Wee drop of malt and one tea loudly swallowed by clergyman

parts.note: the first letter of malt

parts.note: the letter T sounds the same as tea

explanation.surface: A clergyman noisily gulps a drop of whisky and a cup of tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wee drop' looks like a small dram of whisky, but Wee is the definition, a verb meaning to urinate.
explanation.definitionFit: Micturate is the formal medical verb for urinating, and wee is the informal word for the same act.

clue.text: Computer factory with article for Etonian PM

parts.note: a Mac is an Apple computer
a mill is a factory
an is the indefinite article, added on

explanation.surface: A computer plant and a newspaper article about a former Prime Minister who went to Eton.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton is an exclusive English boarding school that has educated many Prime Ministers.
explanation.definitionFit: Harold Macmillan, Prime Minister from 1957 to 1963, was educated at Eton College.

taken as written

explanation.definitionFit: Dionysus is the Greek god of wine and ecstatic festivity, whose worshippers held wild drunken rites.

clue.text: One in yellow family of monkeys trapped by kid

indicators.note: something trapped is held inside, so the monkeys go within the kid

parts.note: a son is a kid
a monkey is a mischievous child, as is an imp

explanation.surface: A member of a family of yellow primates caught by a child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Family of monkeys' wants to be a zoological group; the family is the cartoon one, drawn with yellow skin.
explanation.definitionFit: The Simpsons are the cartoon family of Springfield, drawn with bright yellow skin, so any member is a Simpson.

clue.text: Impressive standing in court, having smuggled yen

indicators.note: something smuggled is hidden inside, so the longing goes within the court

explanation.definitionFit: Cachet means prestige, the distinction that wins admiration, which is an impressive standing in society.

clue.text: Rum comes out in parties, or a French red?

explanation.definitionFit: Eurocommunism was the Western European communist movement of the 1970s, strong in France and Italy, so a French red is an example.

clue.text: Indian side, occasionally erratic, getting cheers

clue.text: Biscuit and a doughnut separately eaten by French bigwig

taken as written
